collection_notes: Steps 1-5 were run identically for every candidate in the US Senate, US House 1-6 and Governor races (the shared WebSearch budget ran out once mid-run and the remaining searches were completed after it reset). To keep effort equal, no T3 items are included for any candidate in these races: every item comes from the T1 voters' pamphlet, official .gov pages or official roll-call pages; promising T3 results are named in these notes for possible later, race-wide use. Campaign websites are recorded from the pamphlet but were not fetched for positions, for any candidate. oregonlive.com and apnews.com are rejected by the search proxy as allowed_domains, so step 5 used three fixed domain groups for everyone: (opb, oregoncapitalchronicle, wweek, ballotpedia), (kgw, koin, kptv, katu), (portlandmercury, vote411, pamplinmedia, portlandtribune). The Multnomah military/overseas online voters' guide was checked and contains no federal or governor statements. Pamphlet excerpts were obtained through a summarizing fetch limited to ~125-character quotes, so excerpts are short. incumbent=false because the pamphlet edition cited in incumbent_source_url lists another candidate in this race as the sitting officeholder. Pamphlet (Lane edition) lists DeSpain as Republican, Libertarian; matches inventory. 'USAF, 30 years, JAG' is her pamphlet prior-governmental-experience entry. Step 5 surfaced a VOTE411 'Oregon US House District 4' candidate page (onyourballot.vote411.org ... id=68146839) and 2024-cycle OPB candidate interviews for all three CD4 candidates; not fetched, to keep T3 treatment identical across all assigned races (cycle/year of the VOTE411 page unconfirmed).
